**brief:** the history probes (`history-fallback`, `cand-k-commit-patch`) look a commit up by the version a question quotes (`3.10`, `v5.3.0`) before its words — the commit the exact release tag points at, then the subjects sharing the prompt's other words — where they used to drop the digits and name a neighbour ("which commit dropped support for Python 3.10" named a 2016 commit), and a merge they pick now shows its patch against its first parent instead of an empty combined diff.
